correctness.rationale: For strict rather than randomized ties, adding voter 2m to an odd electorate loses exactly the event of m correct votes in the old electorate and a final incorrect vote; adding voter 2m+1 to an even electorate gains exactly the old tie followed by a correct vote. Adding two voters to the even electorate gains from m old successes followed by two successes, and loses from m+1 old successes followed by two failures. This gives the frozen conditional increment; tilting the Beta law by u^(m+1)(1-u)^m gives the strictly positive numerator m(alpha-beta)+alpha+2m+1. A2=E[Theta^2]<p. Dominated convergence and reflection of the beta density about 1/2 give L-p=integral over (1/2,1) of (1-u)(f(u)-f(1-u))>0, so at most one even tie and a finite first strict exceedance follow. At (2,1) the mass is 2(k+1)/((n+1)(n+2)); summing it gives both frozen formulas, equality at 8 and A10=15/22. This proof handles all stated real shape parameters. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For any Bernoulli mixture, if T_m is its even tie probability then A_{2m}=A_{2m-1}-T_m/2 by binomial exchangeability (among 2m tied outcomes, the last voter is incorrect with probability one half). Thus fair-tie even accuracy is equivalent to preceding odd accuracy; strict-tie even accuracy is not identical but has an explicit correction.
